what_its_for: Fat emulsions are given through a vein (IV) to provide your body with important fats and calories when you cannot eat enough food by mouth. They are used when you need nutrition support, such as after surgery, during serious illness, or when your digestive system is not working properly. They also provide essential fatty acids that your body needs to stay healthy.
how_to_take: This medicine is always given by a nurse or doctor through an IV line directly into your vein. You should never try to give this to yourself at home unless you have been specially trained by your healthcare team and have been set up for home infusion. The liquid will drip slowly into your vein over several hours. Tell your nurse right away if you feel any burning, pain, swelling, or redness at the IV site.
dosing: Your doctor will decide exactly how much fat emulsion you need based on your weight, age, health condition, and how many calories your body needs each day. The infusion usually runs slowly over 12 to 24 hours. Do not try to change the drip speed on your own. Your healthcare team will check your blood regularly to make sure you are getting the right amount.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by healthcare professionals in a hospital or home infusion setting, missed doses are managed by your care team. If you are on a home infusion program and you miss or skip an infusion, call your home infusion nurse or doctor right away for instructions. Do not try to make up a missed dose by running the infusion faster.
storage: Fat emulsions must be stored in a cool place, typically between 36°F and 77°F (2°C and 25°C). Keep the bags away from direct light and do not freeze them. Once a bag has been opened or connected to your IV line, it must be used within the time frame your pharmacist or nurse tells you, usually within 12 to 24 hours. Always check the bag before use — if the liquid looks separated, discolored, or has particles floating in it, do not use it and contact your pharmacy or nurse.
what_to_avoid: Avoid letting the IV bag hang for longer than your nurse or pharmacist has instructed. Do not mix other medicines into the fat emulsion bag unless your pharmacist has specifically approved it. Avoid touching or adjusting the IV tubing or pump settings without guidance from your healthcare team. Let your doctor know if you eat a high-fat diet or take any herbal supplements, as these may affect your treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or nurse right away if you notice any of these warning signs: fever, chills, or shaking during the infusion; chest pain or trouble breathing; dizziness or feeling faint; severe headache; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); swelling of your face, lips, or throat; unusual bruising or bleeding; pain, redness, or swelling at the IV site; or if the IV bag looks cloudy, has particles in it, or separates into layers. These could be signs of a serious reaction.
when_it_works: Fat emulsions start providing your body with calories and essential fats right away during the infusion. However, you may not feel a noticeable difference immediately. Your healthcare team will monitor your blood tests and overall health over days to weeks to see how well the nutrition support is working. Improvement in your energy and healing depends on your overall health and medical condition.
special_populations: Premature babies and newborns: Fat emulsions are used carefully in premature infants and newborns, with very close monitoring because their bodies process fat differently. Special formulations may be used for babies. Older adults: Elderly patients may need lower doses and closer monitoring of blood fat levels and liver function. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Patients with liver disease, kidney disease, blood clotting problems, or very high blood fat levels (hyperlipidemia) require extra caution and frequent blood tests. Always tell your entire healthcare team about all your health conditions.
